reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) discusses general entropy stabilization in high-entropy materials and synthesis challenges of HEA nanoparticles, but none provides specific data on surface diffusion, premelting, or comparative melting behavior in nanoparticles. The key premises about surface defect-driven diffusion and core entropy stabilization during premelting are therefore unsupported by the referenced passages.
premises: High surface energy and nanoscale synthesis defects promote enhanced surface atomic diffusion in HEA nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy in the multi-element core stabilizes the ordered structure against melting.
The competition between surface disordering and core stabilization governs premelting behavior.
HEA nanoparticles will show a more pronounced premelt layer and disorder gradient than mono/binary alloy nanoparticles of similar size.
